title: Dispatch: source-clause semantic IR and completeness contracts (attempt 1)
description:
SUPERVISOR PRE-PLANNING. Implement exactly what is specified here. Read the
parent spec first: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1`, including its DESIGN section —
the scope guard there is binding.

=== SCOPE: DESIGN + TYPE CONTRACTS ONLY ===
The parent carries a TYPE GUARD: it may remain a task only while it is strictly
an ADR / schema-contract deliverable. This dispatch therefore delivers the
contract and its types and NOTHING ELSE. Do not touch the importer, do not
modify any existing projector, do not migrate any record, do not regenerate the
pack. Those belong to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.2, .19.3.*, .19.4.* and .19.6.1.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts
Do NOT edit packages/core/src/internal.ts — a sibling dispatch conventionally
owns it and export promotion is deferred to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.5. Your test
imports the new modules by relative path ('../src/rules/clauseIr/index.js'),
which is the established convention in packages/core/test.

=== WHAT TO BUILD ===

1. ADR 0020. It REFINES ADR 0017 — read docs/adr/0017-*.md and
   docs/rules-pack-compiler.md first and reference them explicitly. State:

   * The semantic unit is a source-backed CLAUSE, not a record. Records become
     materialized views that group clauses, with no loss of the current
     consumer surface.
   * The FOUR INDEPENDENT DIMENSIONS that replace the single overloaded word
     "modeled": CAPTURED (source text present), PROJECTED (structured fields
     exist), SUPPORTED (an engine capability can execute it), DISCOVERABLE
     (runtime lookup can find the canonical clause). They are orthogonal. A
     clause can be captured and projected yet unsupported and undiscoverable.
     No gate may collapse them into one verdict.
   * The scope guard, faithfully: the universal layer is ONLY clause identity,
     semantic ownership, completeness requirements, alternatives and branching,
     provenance, capability requirements, and readiness state. It explicitly
     PERMITS shared normalized primitives, kind-specific composition on top of
     them, curated source-backed specifications, and explicit
     unsupported/adjudicated clauses. It is NOT a universal rules DSL and does
     not require every D&D mechanic to compile into one generic runtime
     language.
   * THE DECISIVE RULE: when a projector recognizes that a deterministic clause
     exists but cannot completely represent it, it MUST emit an explicit
     INCOMPLETE clause and fail the appropriate gate. It must never produce a
     superficially valid partial record. Silent partial projection is the one
     forbidden behavior.
   * Why completeness cannot be judged from atom presence — it is evaluated
     against the clause KIND's contract. Ground this in the 2026-07-24 audit
     evidence: alternative damage modes stored as parallel damage, recharge
     triggers read as reset periods, partial saves treated as complete,
     legendary actions with no budget or cost, option mechanics hoisted onto
     parent features, typed records missing branching/timing/termination.

2. packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts — the IR expressed as TypeScript
   types. Every clause carries: stable clause identity; exact source span or
   spans; semantic owner and record owner; clause kind; trigger and eligibility
   predicates; activation / action-economy cost; targets and geometry; checks,
   attacks, saves, and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ALTERNATIVES; success, failure and
   partial-success branches; damage, healing, grants, ledger changes and state
   transitions; duration, recurrence, repeat checks, immunity windows and
   termination; execution owner and required engine capabilities; readiness
   disposition; regression evidence.
   Model INCOMPLETENESS as a first-class state, never as an absence: an
   incomplete clause names which contract requirement it fails and why.
   Required-capability values use the qualified engine:F1..engine:F10 form.

3. packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts — the completeness contracts as
   DATA, not prose, with a pure evaluator.
   Contracts required for at least: attacks, saves, checks, branches, action
   economy, resources, durations, state transitions, geometry, choices,
   variants, entity lifecycles, ledgers, and model adjudication.
   A documented clause-completeness schema is required for every one of the
   fifteen mechanics-bearing record families: rule, feature, spell, creature,
   hazard, equipment, magic-item, ancestry, background, condition, action, feat,
   class, subclass, table.
   The evaluator takes a clause plus its contract and returns complete, or
   incomplete with named reasons. It must be structurally impossible to reach
   "complete" from atom presence alone.

4. packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts. Assert at minimum:
   * every one of the fifteen record families has a registered contract;
   * every contract names its required clause kinds;
   * the four dimensions are independently representable, and a clause that is
     CAPTURED + PROJECTED but not SUPPORTED does not evaluate complete;
   * a clause with every atom present but a missing required branch evaluates
     INCOMPLETE with a named reason — this is the anti-silent-partial-projection
     regression and is the most important test in the file;
   * a projector that cannot fully represent a deterministic clause can express
     that ONLY as an explicit incomplete clause.
   Use small hand-built fixtures. Do NOT load the 7.4 MB rules pack; this bead
   is a contract, not a migration.

=== NAMING HAZARD — READ BEFORE WRITING ANY IDENTIFIER ===
"F1".."F10" means THREE different things in this repository:
  engine:F1..F10    pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1..F8      Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01..F-35   Opus 5 audit findings
  sol:CAP-001..014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001..012    independent review findings (renamed from SOL-*)
Never write a bare "F5" or a bare "CAP-002". Always qualify with the prefix.
The CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t used yet another F1-F10 taxonomy that does NOT
correspond to engine:F1-F10 except loosely at F2/F3/F5/F7.

=== COUNT HYGIENE ===
No test and no committed artifact may depend on a hand-copied number (391, 399,
77, 79, 794, 1016, 1813). Every count is a SNAPSHOT of commit 4384f25. Where a
count matters, commit the QUERY that generates it and let the number be derived
at run time.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` in this worktree FIRST. Worktrees have no node_modules of their
own and will otherwise resolve @eshyra/core through the parent checkout's stale
dist/*.d.ts and report phantom typecheck errors.
Then run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files
(Biome formats and organizes imports), so verifying after committing means the
committed tree is not the tree that passed.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under "FILES YOU OWN". Two sibling dispatches are
  running in parallel right now on disjoint file sets. Touching anything else —
  especially package.json, packages/core/package.json, or
  packages/core/src/internal.ts — will collide with them. If you believe you
  need a file outside your list, record that in your completion notes instead
  and stop short of editing it.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`. If you
  discover follow-up work, use `bd create` and say so in your notes.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a pull request, do NOT merge.
  AGENTS.md's standing push authority does not apply to you on this dispatch;
  integration belongs to the agent that dispatched you. Committed work on your
  branch is a complete handoff.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete any existing test or audit expectation.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.
acceptance_criteria:
• ADR 0020 exists, refines ADR 0017, and states the clause unit, the four independent dimensions, the scope guard, and the decisive rule.
• Clause IR types cover every field listed in the parent bead, with incompleteness as a first-class state.
• Completeness contracts exist as data for all listed clause kinds and all fifteen record families.
• The evaluator cannot return complete from atom presence alone, and a test proves it.
• npm run verify:worktree passes from this worktree.
• No file outside the owned list is modified.
